classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught square identities to complete terms; the final part requires a simple rewrite of the divided sum before expansion.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly expands a perfect square using those identities. The closest catalogue skill is expand-simplify-special-products; fractional terms in i–l retain the same method.
questions.methodNote: Page 6 derives (a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2 and (a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2. Example 1 substitutes complete terms into these identities before simplifying. Page 7 reinforces perfect-square expansion.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct application of perfect-square identities, including coefficients and fractional terms.

classification.difficultyReason: Expand squared binomials and products, then subtract complete expansions with correct signs.

questions.mappingNote: Each part combines a squared binomial with a subtracted product or squared binomial. Expand using the taught identities and distributive law, retain brackets around the subtracted expansion, then collect like terms.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Expand squared binomials and products, then subtract complete expansions with correct signs.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose a nearby convenient number and express each base as a sum or difference, following the taught numerical-square method.

questions.methodNote: Page 6 establishes both perfect-square identities. Page 7 Example 2 evaluates 99 squared by writing it as (100-1) squared and retaining substitution, numerical expansion and final evaluation.
